_README: Literature H2 surface dissociation rate-constant laws, kd = kd0 exp(-Ed / RT) (J = kd P).
Same layout as literature_diffusivity.json. surface_rates_plot.py draws it (literature only);
diffusivity_plot.load_dissociation_literature reads it.
Top-level keys are materials, named as in a paper ('316L SS', 'Hastelloy N',
'NiO'). A run folder finds its key by its name without the H count and
without the structure words '_supercell', '_bestsqs' and '_sqs': folder
'Al_supercell_10H' looks for 'Al', 'HastelloyN_bestsqs_5H' for 'Hastelloy N'.
Matching ignores case, spaces, underscores and hyphens. A run whose name
differs from its key in more than that (a typo, a seed number, 'oxide' for a
formula) is listed in _ALIASES: run-folder name -> key (the same table as in
literature_diffusivity.json).
Any key starting with '_' is documentation (or the alias table) and is not
a material.
Each entry is valid ONLY across its own T_C window - a study measured over
300-600 C is never extrapolated to meet the MD points.
Isotopes: every entry is drawn. A deuterium (D2) law carries a dagger (†) at
the end of its label and a tritium (T2) law an asterisk (*); hydrogen is
unmarked. The 'isotope' field says the same.
Laws read off a published figure (digitised) rather than printed carry
'digitised_from' with the figure, and their note gives the line's ends.
Units are the same for every entry: energies in kJ/mol, and kd0 in the
units its schema names. A value printed in other units is converted and the
printed value kept in 'as_printed'; a law read off a figure is converted from
the reading.

_SCHEMA.label: REQUIRED. Citation as it should appear in the legend, e.g. 'Zhang et al. 2026'.
_SCHEMA.isotope: OPTIONAL. 'H2' (default), 'D2' or 'T2'. The label marks a D2 law with a dagger (†) and a T2 law with an asterisk (*).
_SCHEMA.kd0: REQUIRED. Pre-exponential factor of the dissociation rate constant, as printed in the source.
_SCHEMA.kd0_units: Units of kd0: 'mol/(m2 s Pa)' (default, mol H2) | 'mol H/(m2 s Pa)' | 'atoms/(cm2 s Torr)'; a sticking coefficient goes in 'note'.
_SCHEMA.Ed: REQUIRED. Activation energy of dissociation, as printed in the source.
_SCHEMA.Ed_units: Units of Ed: always 'kJ/mol' in this file. A value printed in other units is converted, and the printed value is kept in 'as_printed'.
_SCHEMA.T_C: REQUIRED (or T_K). Validity range [low, high] in degrees Celsius; null when no range is known: the law is stored but not drawn.
_SCHEMA.T_K: Alternative to T_C: validity range [low, high] in Kelvin.
_SCHEMA.digitised_from: OPTIONAL. Set when the law was read off a published figure instead of printed: the figure it came from. Such laws are named as read off a figure in the plot caption.
_SCHEMA.as_printed: Set when a printed value was converted to this file's units: the value and unit as printed in the source.
_SCHEMA.note: OPTIONAL. Free-text provenance - method, purity, DOI. Not plotted.

Ni.label: Altunoglu et al., 1991 (INL 2020)
Ni.note: Hydrogen (H2) data, from Humrickhouse & Fuerst 2020, Tritium Transport Phenomena in Molten-Salt Reactors: Validation Data Needs and Research Plan, INL/EXT-20-59927 Rev. 0, Idaho National Laboratory, Table 5, ref [32]; values as printed. Original source: A.K. Altunoglu, D.A. Blackburn, N.S.J. Braithwaite, D.M. Grant, Permeation of hydrogen through nickel foils: surface reaction rates at low temperatures, J. Less-Common Met. 172-174 (1991) 718-726, doi:10.1016/0022-5088(91)90195-A. Range 373-623 K from the publisher abstract (doi:10.1016/S0022-5088(06)80312-7, read via Consensus): the experiments ran "for temperatures between 373 K and 623 K" by pressure modulation at 5.3 Pa-7.3 kPa. The abstract prints k1 = 1.44e-6 exp(-29.68e3/RT) mol H2 m-2 s-1 Pa-1, which INL rounds to 1.4e-6 and 30 kJ/mol.

316L SS.label: Guo et al., 2025†
316L SS.note: Deuterium (D2) data, gas-driven permeation through 316L membranes tested at 823, 773, 723, 673, 623, 553 and 473 K (Table 1: 550-200 C); from Guo et al. 2025 (J. Nucl. Mater. 614, 155864; doi:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2025.155864); values as printed. Eq. (31): Kdis0 = (4.88 +/- 1.08)e-7 mol m-2 s-1 Pa-1, Ed = 0.57 +/- 0.1 eV; from the 0.05 mm membrane (surface-controlled, flux linear in pressure), eq. (22); the sticking coefficient is absorbed in Kdis.

316 SS.label: Grant et al., 1988 (ion-beam cleaned)
316 SS.note: Read off Guo et al. 2025 (J. Nucl. Mater. 614, 155864; doi:10.1016/j.jnucmat.2025.155864), Fig. 8(d), whose y-axis is dissociation (the paper's caption swaps (c) and (d)), the line '316 ion beam clean, Grant, D. M.': digitised from the figure, not printed. Original source: D.M. Grant et al., Hydrogen in 316 steel - diffusion, permeation and surface reaction, J. Nucl. Mater. 152 (1988) 139-145 (Guo's ref [32]). Isotope as in that paper's title. The line runs over 1000/T = 1.388-1.981 with log10 values -7.35 to -9.85. Reading Guo's own lines the same way gives their printed laws to within 0.003 eV and 7 % in the pre-factor. The line runs off the top of the plot, so its high-temperature end (above about 450 C) is not visible and the range is cut there. The same law as Grant's recombination line in Fig. 8(c); check against Grant et al. 1988.
